clips.send: Common mix-up: Spiders are not insects. Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts; spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Spiders are not insects. Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts; spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts.

clips.send: Sponges. e.g. tube sponge, bath sponge. The simplest animals: no tissues, organs, head or symmetry. Water flows in through thousands of pores; cells filter out tiny bits of food. Adults stay attached to rocks on the sea floor and don’t move.
clips.text: Sponges. e.g. tube sponge, bath sponge. The simplest animals: no tissues, organs, head or symmetry.. Water flows in through thousands of pores; cells filter out tiny bits of food.. Adults stay attached to rocks on the sea floor and don’t move.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Octopuses and squid are mollusks even though they have no outer shell.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Octopuses and squid are mollusks even though they have no outer shell.

clips.send: Echinoderms. e.g. sea star, sea urchin, sand dollar. Spiny skin and five-part radial symmetry as adults (their larvae are bilateral!). Hundreds of tiny tube feet, moved by water pressure, help them crawl and grip. Many can regrow lost arms. They live only in the ocean.
clips.text: Echinoderms. e.g. sea star, sea urchin, sand dollar. Spiny skin and five-part radial symmetry as adults (their larvae are bilateral!).. Hundreds of tiny tube feet, moved by water pressure, help them crawl and grip.. Many can regrow lost arms. They live only in the ocean.

clips.send: Arthropods. e.g. ants, spiders, crabs, centipedes. A hard exoskeleton covers the body; it must be shed (molted) for the animal to grow. Jointed legs and a segmented body. The biggest animal group: more than 3 out of 4 known animal species are arthropods.
clips.text: Arthropods. e.g. ants, spiders, crabs, centipedes. A hard exoskeleton covers the body; it must be shed (molted) for the animal to grow.. Jointed legs and a segmented body.. The biggest animal group: more than 3 out of 4 known animal species are arthropods.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A hard shell or exoskeleton is not a backbone. Crabs and snails are invertebrates.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A hard shell or exoskeleton is not a backbone. Crabs and snails are invertebrates.

clips.send: Backbone (spine). a feature, not a group. A chain of small bones called vertebrae that protects the spinal cord. Animals with a backbone are vertebrates. Only about 5 percent of animal species have one! A backbone is part of an internal skeleton, which grows along with the body.
clips.text: Backbone (spine). a feature, not a group. A chain of small bones called vertebrae that protects the spinal cord.. Animals with a backbone are vertebrates. Only about 5% of animal species have one!. A backbone is part of an internal skeleton, which grows along with the body.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Sponges look like plants, but they are animals: they can’t make food, they eat it.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Sponges look like plants, but they are animals: they can’t make food, they eat it.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish: they breathe air with lungs and nurse their young.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish: they breathe air with lungs and nurse their young.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Bats fly but are mammals; penguins can’t fly but are birds. Feathers, not flight, define a bird.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Bats fly but are mammals; penguins can’t fly but are birds. Feathers, not flight, define a bird.

clips.send: Common mix-up: “Worm” is not one group: flatworms, roundworms and segmented worms are separate phyla. Snakes and caterpillars are not worms!
clips.text: Common mix-up: “Worm” is not one group: flatworms, roundworms and segmented worms are separate phyla. Snakes and caterpillars are not worms!

clips.send: Cnidarians. e.g. jellyfish, coral, sea anemone, hydra. Radial symmetry, like spokes on a wheel. Tentacles carry stinging cells that capture prey. Only one body opening: food goes in and waste comes out of the same mouth.
clips.text: Cnidarians. e.g. jellyfish, coral, sea anemone, hydra. Radial symmetry, like spokes on a wheel.. Tentacles carry stinging cells that capture prey.. Only one body opening: food goes in and waste comes out of the same mouth.

clips.send: Fish. e.g. salmon, shark, clownfish. Gills take dissolved oxygen out of water. Scales protect the body; fins steer and balance. About half of all vertebrate species are fish. Most lay eggs in water.
clips.text: Fish. e.g. salmon, shark, clownfish. Gills take dissolved oxygen out of water.. Scales protect the body; fins steer and balance.. About half of all vertebrate species are fish. Most lay eggs in water.

clips.send: Amphibians. e.g. frog, toad, salamander. “Double life”: young (tadpoles) live in water with gills; adults usually live on land with lungs. Thin, moist skin with no scales; adults also breathe through their skin. Lay jelly-coated eggs in water and go through metamorphosis.
clips.text: Amphibians. e.g. frog, toad, salamander. “Double life”: young (tadpoles) live in water with gills; adults usually live on land with lungs.. Thin, moist skin with no scales; adults also breathe through their skin.. Lay jelly-coated eggs in water and go through metamorphosis.

clips.send: Worms. e.g. earthworm (segmented), planarian (flat), roundworm. Bilateral symmetry with a head end. That’s where nerves and senses gather. An earthworm’s body is made of about 100–150 ring-shaped segments. Earthworms breathe through their moist skin and mix air into soil.
clips.text: Worms. e.g. earthworm (segmented), planarian (flat), roundworm. Bilateral symmetry with a head end. That’s where nerves and senses gather.. An earthworm’s body is made of about 100–150 ring-shaped segments.. Earthworms breathe through their moist skin and mix air into soil.

clips.send: Birds. e.g. robin, eagle, penguin, ostrich. Feathers: only birds have them. They insulate and help with flight. Hollow, lightweight bones and a beak with no teeth. Endotherms that lay hard-shelled eggs.
clips.text: Birds. e.g. robin, eagle, penguin, ostrich. Feathers: only birds have them. They insulate and help with flight.. Hollow, lightweight bones and a beak with no teeth.. Endotherms that lay hard-shelled eggs.

clips.send: Mollusks. e.g. snail, clam, octopus, squid. Soft body; most have a hard shell made by a layer called the mantle. Many move on one big muscular foot. The octopus is one of the smartest invertebrates; it can solve puzzles.
clips.text: Mollusks. e.g. snail, clam, octopus, squid. Soft body; most have a hard shell made by a layer called the mantle.. Many move on one big muscular foot.. The octopus is one of the smartest invertebrates; it can solve puzzles.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A starfish is not a fish! Scientists prefer the name “sea star”.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A starfish is not a fish! Scientists prefer the name “sea star”.

clips.send: Reptiles. e.g. lizard, snake, turtle, crocodile. Dry, scaly skin that keeps water in. Breathe with lungs their whole life. Lay eggs with leathery shells on land, so they don’t need water to reproduce.
clips.text: Reptiles. e.g. lizard, snake, turtle, crocodile. Dry, scaly skin that keeps water in.. Breathe with lungs their whole life.. Lay eggs with leathery shells on land, so they don’t need water to reproduce.

clips.send: Mammals. e.g. fox, whale, bat, human. Hair or fur, at least at some point in life. Mothers feed their young with milk. Endotherms; most give birth to live young (the platypus lays eggs!).
clips.text: Mammals. e.g. fox, whale, bat, human. Hair or fur, at least at some point in life.. Mothers feed their young with milk.. Endotherms; most give birth to live young (the platypus lays eggs!).

clips.send: 鱼类。例：鲑鱼、鲨鱼、小丑鱼。用鳃从水中摄取溶解的氧气。鳞片保护身体，鳍用来控制方向和保持平衡。大约一半的脊椎动物物种是鱼类，大多数在水中产卵。
clips.text: 鱼类. 例：鲑鱼、鲨鱼、小丑鱼. 用鳃从水中摄取溶解的氧气。. 鳞片保护身体，鳍用来控制方向和保持平衡。. 大约一半的脊椎动物物种是鱼类，大多数在水中产卵。

clips.send: 容易混淆：蜘蛛不是昆虫。昆虫有 6 条足、3 个体段；蜘蛛有 8 条足、2 个体段。
clips.text: 容易混淆：蜘蛛不是昆虫。昆虫有 6 条足、3 个体段；蜘蛛有 8 条足、2 个体段。

clips.send: 容易混淆：章鱼和鱿鱼虽然没有外壳，但也是软体动物。
clips.text: 容易混淆：章鱼和鱿鱼虽然没有外壳，但也是软体动物。

clips.send: 爬行动物。例：蜥蜴、蛇、龟、鳄鱼。皮肤干燥、有鳞，能防止体内水分散失。一生都用肺呼吸。在陆地上产下有革质卵壳的卵，繁殖不再依赖水。
clips.text: 爬行动物. 例：蜥蜴、蛇、龟、鳄鱼. 皮肤干燥、有鳞，能防止体内水分散失。. 一生都用肺呼吸。. 在陆地上产下有革质卵壳的卵，繁殖不再依赖水。

clips.send: 脊柱。一种特征，而不是一个类群。由许多块叫做椎骨的小骨头连成，保护里面的脊髓。有脊柱的动物叫脊椎动物，只占动物物种的大约 百分之5!。脊柱是内骨骼的一部分，会随着身体一起生长。
clips.text: 脊柱. 一种特征，而不是一个类群. 由许多块叫做椎骨的小骨头连成，保护里面的脊髓。. 有脊柱的动物叫脊椎动物，只占动物物种的大约 5%!. 脊柱是内骨骼的一部分，会随着身体一起生长。

clips.send: 棘皮动物。例：海星、海胆、海参。皮肤上有棘，成体呈五辐射对称（而幼体是两侧对称的！）。数百个小小的管足靠水压运动，帮助它们爬行和吸附。很多棘皮动物能再生失去的腕。它们只生活在海洋中。

clips.send: 鸟类。例：知更鸟、鹰、企鹅、鸵鸟。羽毛：只有鸟类才有，能保温并帮助飞行。骨骼中空、很轻，有喙而没有牙齿。恒温动物，产硬壳卵。
clips.text: 鸟类. 例：知更鸟、鹰、企鹅、鸵鸟. 羽毛：只有鸟类才有，能保温并帮助飞行。. 骨骼中空、很轻，有喙而没有牙齿。. 恒温动物，产硬壳卵。

clips.send: 容易混淆：坚硬的外壳或外骨骼不是脊柱。螃蟹和蜗牛都是无脊椎动物。
clips.text: 容易混淆：坚硬的外壳或外骨骼不是脊柱。螃蟹和蜗牛都是无脊椎动物。

clips.send: 两栖动物。例：青蛙、蟾蜍、蝾螈。“两种生活”：幼体（蝌蚪）生活在水中，用鳃呼吸；成体大多生活在陆地上，用肺呼吸。皮肤薄而湿润，没有鳞片；成体还能用皮肤辅助呼吸。在水中产下包着胶质的卵，要经过变态发育。
clips.text: 两栖动物. 例：青蛙、蟾蜍、蝾螈. “两种生活”：幼体（蝌蚪）生活在水中，用鳃呼吸；成体大多生活在陆地上，用肺呼吸。. 皮肤薄而湿润，没有鳞片；成体还能用皮肤辅助呼吸。. 在水中产下包着胶质的卵，要经过变态发育。

clips.send: 哺乳动物。例：狐狸、鲸、蝙蝠、人。身上有毛发（至少在一生中的某个阶段有）。母亲用乳汁哺育幼崽。恒温动物；大多数是胎生的（鸭嘴兽却是卵生的！）。
clips.text: 哺乳动物. 例：狐狸、鲸、蝙蝠、人. 身上有毛发（至少在一生中的某个阶段有）。. 母亲用乳汁哺育幼崽。. 恒温动物；大多数是胎生的（鸭嘴兽却是卵生的！）。

clips.send: 容易混淆：蝙蝠会飞，却是哺乳动物；企鹅不会飞，却是鸟。决定是不是鸟的是羽毛，而不是会不会飞。

clips.send: 容易混淆：海绵看起来像植物，但它是动物：它不能自己制造食物，而是要“吃”食物。
clips.text: 容易混淆：海绵看起来像植物，但它是动物：它不能自己制造食物，而是要“吃”食物。

clips.send: 海绵动物。例：管状海绵、浴海绵。最简单的动物：没有组织和器官，没有头，也没有对称性。水从成千上万个小孔流进身体，细胞从水中滤出细小的食物。成体固着在海底的岩石上，不会移动。
clips.text: 海绵动物. 例：管状海绵、浴海绵. 最简单的动物：没有组织和器官，没有头，也没有对称性。. 水从成千上万个小孔流进身体，细胞从水中滤出细小的食物。. 成体固着在海底的岩石上，不会移动。

clips.send: 刺胞动物（腔肠动物）。例：水母、珊瑚虫、海葵、水螅。辐射对称，像车轮的辐条。触手上有刺细胞，用来捕捉猎物。身体只有一个开口：食物从口进入，残渣也从口排出。
clips.text: 刺胞动物（腔肠动物）. 例：水母、珊瑚虫、海葵、水螅. 辐射对称，像车轮的辐条。. 触手上有刺细胞，用来捕捉猎物。. 身体只有一个开口：食物从口进入，残渣也从口排出。

clips.send: 节肢动物。例：蚂蚁、蜘蛛、螃蟹、蜈蚣。坚硬的外骨骼包住身体，动物必须蜕皮才能长大。附肢分节，身体也分节。动物界最大的类群：已知的动物物种中，超过四分之三是节肢动物。
clips.text: 节肢动物. 例：蚂蚁、蜘蛛、螃蟹、蜈蚣. 坚硬的外骨骼包住身体，动物必须蜕皮才能长大。. 附肢分节，身体也分节。. 动物界最大的类群：已知的动物物种中，超过四分之三是节肢动物。

clips.send: 软体动物。例：蜗牛、蛤、章鱼、鱿鱼。身体柔软，大多数有由外套膜分泌形成的硬壳。许多软体动物靠一个肌肉发达的足来运动。章鱼是最聪明的无脊椎动物之一，能解开谜题。

clips.send: 容易混淆：鲸和海豚是哺乳动物，不是鱼：它们用肺呼吸空气，并用乳汁哺育幼崽。

clips.send: 蠕虫。例：蚯蚓（环节动物）、涡虫（扁形动物）、蛔虫（线虫动物）。两侧对称，有头端，神经和感觉器官集中在那里。蚯蚓的身体由大约 100 到 150 个环状体节组成。蚯蚓靠湿润的体表呼吸，还能疏松土壤。
clips.text: 蠕虫. 例：蚯蚓（环节动物）、涡虫（扁形动物）、蛔虫（线虫动物）. 两侧对称，有头端，神经和感觉器官集中在那里。. 蚯蚓的身体由大约 100 到 150 个环状体节组成。. 蚯蚓靠湿润的体表呼吸，还能疏松土壤。

clips.send: 容易混淆：“蠕虫”不是一个分类单位：扁形动物、线虫动物和环节动物是不同的门。蛇和毛毛虫都不是蠕虫！
